title: 264. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Polynomial Zeros and Multiplicity on Graphs
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Identifying the Multiplicity of a Zero from Factored Form
questions.learningObjective: Determine the multiplicity of a zero from the exponent of its factor.
questions.question: For \(f(x)=(x-3)^2(x+1)\), what is the multiplicity of the zero \(x=3\)?
questions.explanation: The zero \(x=3\) comes from the factor \((x-3)\), which has exponent \(2\). Therefore the multiplicity of the zero \(x=3\) is \(2\). Option A is correct.
questions.hint: The multiplicity of a zero is the exponent on its corresponding factor.

questions.concept: Graph Behavior at a Zero of Even Multiplicity
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a graph crosses or touches the \(x\)-axis at a zero of even multiplicity.
questions.question: The graph of \(f(x)=(x-2)^4\) meets the \(x\)-axis at \(x=2\). What does the graph do at this zero?

options.label: A
options.text: It touches the \(x\)-axis and turns around.

questions.explanation: The zero \(x=2\) has multiplicity \(4\), which is even. A zero of even multiplicity makes the graph touch the \(x\)-axis and turn around without crossing. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Find the multiplicity of the zero and decide whether it is even or odd.

questions.concept: Graph Behavior at a Zero of Odd Multiplicity
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a graph crosses or touches the \(x\)-axis at a zero of odd multiplicity.
questions.question: The graph of \(f(x)=(x+1)^3\) meets the \(x\)-axis at \(x=-1\). What does the graph do at this zero?

options.label: A
options.text: It touches the \(x\)-axis and turns around.

questions.explanation: The zero \(x=-1\) has multiplicity \(3\), which is odd. A zero of odd multiplicity makes the graph cross the \(x\)-axis. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Find the multiplicity of the zero and decide whether it is even or odd.

questions.concept: Identifying the Zero with a Given Multiplicity
questions.learningObjective: Identify which zero has a specified multiplicity from factored form.
questions.question: For \(f(x)=x^2(x-5)^3\), which zero has multiplicity \(3\)?
questions.explanation: The factor \(x^2\) gives the zero \(x=0\) with multiplicity \(2\). The factor \((x-5)^3\) gives the zero \(x=5\) with multiplicity \(3\). Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Match the exponent to the factor that produces the zero.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the degree of a polynomial from the sum of the multiplicities of its zeros.
questions.question: For \(f(x)=(x-1)^2(x+2)^3(x-4)\), what is the degree of the polynomial?
questions.explanation: The multiplicities of the zeros are \(2\), \(3\), and \(1\). Their sum is \(2+3+1=6\). The degree of the polynomial equals the sum of the multiplicities of its zeros. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Add the exponents of all linear factors to find the degree.

questions.concept: Matching Graph Behavior to a Polynomial
questions.learningObjective: Select the polynomial that matches given behavior at two zeros.
questions.question: A polynomial graph touches the \(x\)-axis at \(x=3\) and crosses the \(x\)-axis at \(x=-1\). Which polynomial could represent this graph?
questions.explanation: Touching at \(x=3\) requires even multiplicity, so the factor \((x-3)\) must have an even exponent such as \(2\). Crossing at \(x=-1\) requires odd multiplicity, so the factor \((x+1)\) must have an odd exponent such as \(1\). The polynomial \((x-3)^2(x+1)\) matches both behaviors. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Touching means even multiplicity; crossing means odd multiplicity.

questions.learningObjective: Infer a possible multiplicity from a graph that touches the \(x\)-axis.
questions.question: The graph of a polynomial touches the \(x\)-axis at \(x=2\) without crossing it. Which could be the multiplicity of the zero \(x=2\)?
questions.explanation: A graph that touches the \(x\)-axis and turns around has a zero of even multiplicity. Among the choices, \(2\) is even, while \(3\) is odd. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Recall how the parity of a zero's multiplicity affects whether the graph crosses the \(x\)-axis.

questions.concept: Identifying a Zero with Even Multiplicity
questions.learningObjective: Identify which zero has a specified even multiplicity from factored form.
questions.question: For \(f(x)=x(x-1)^2(x+3)^4\), which zero has multiplicity \(4\)?
questions.explanation: The factor \((x+3)^4\) gives the zero \(x=-3\) with multiplicity \(4\). The factor \((x-1)^2\) gives \(x=1\) with multiplicity \(2\). Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Look for the factor whose exponent is \(4\).

questions.concept: Total Number of Zeros Counted with Multiplicity
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the sum of multiplicities for all zeros of a polynomial.
questions.question: For \(f(x)=(x+2)^4(x-1)(x-3)^3\), what is the total number of zeros counted with multiplicity?
questions.explanation: The multiplicities are \(4\), \(1\), and \(3\). Their sum is \(4+1+3=8\). Therefore the total number of zeros counted with multiplicity is \(8\), so option A is correct. Option B counts only the \(3\) distinct zeros \(x=-2\), \(x=1\), and \(x=3\) and ignores their multiplicities.
questions.hint: Add all exponents from the linear factors.

questions.concept: Matching Multiplicity Behavior at Multiple Zeros
questions.learningObjective: Select the polynomial that matches crossing, touching, and flattening behavior at given zeros.
questions.question: A polynomial graph crosses the \(x\)-axis at \(x=-1\), touches the \(x\)-axis at \(x=2\), and crosses with a flattening behavior at \(x=4\). Which polynomial could represent this graph?
questions.explanation: Crossing at \(x=-1\) requires odd multiplicity, so \((x+1)\) has exponent \(1\). Touching at \(x=2\) requires even multiplicity, so \((x-2)\) has exponent \(2\). Crossing with flattening at \(x=4\) requires odd multiplicity greater than \(1\), such as exponent \(3\), so \((x-4)^3\) is appropriate. The polynomial \((x+1)(x-2)^2(x-4)^3\) matches all three behaviors. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Flattening while crossing indicates odd multiplicity greater than \(1\).
